decisions.reason: As an evolved and renamed version of an already accepted trommel screen, it appears to build on a proven platform with limited incremental carrying cost, so the option value of keeping it remains attractive.
The 2019 update of the whole AK series to EU Stage V suggests this is a strategically maintained core line rather than a tentative experiment, making withdrawal within a year unlikely.

Its move from a mention in 2018 to a dedicated page in 2019 indicates enough promise to continue, but thinner evidence and overlap with other grinder experiments keep the abandonment risk comparatively high.
The CERON generation was presented as setting benchmarks and was backed by a concrete use case, so for an established German machinery maker it looks like a valuable option worth retaining.
